# t-006: tmux layout engine: columns, per-column tabs, keymap, hint bar, ToS guard

## Description
Create and manage the tmux session that hosts everything. It has two visible columns (planners left, implementers right), a status pane at the bottom running the Textual status app (t-007/t-008), and a persistent key-hint status line. Each column shows one agent at a time. Its other agents live in a hidden *stash* window and are swapped in and out to act as tabs. Mouse support uses tmux `mouse on`.

The engine must uphold the ToS guardrails: AI CLI panes are only ever created (with argv from t-005), moved, resized, focused, or killed. tandem never sends keys to them and never reads their content.

## Requirement Classification
- **Type**: New Feature
- **Rationale**: Core multiplexer capability.
- **Regression Risk**: Low (new code). Must not break the user's existing tmux sessions: use a dedicated socket (`tmux -L tandem`) and config (`-f` tandem-owned file).

## Code Structure Diagram
```text
tandem/src/tandem/tmux/
├── client.py    # TmuxClient(socket="tandem"); run(args) -> result; allow-list of subcommands per pane kind
├── layout.py    # build(): session, columns, status pane, stash window; reflow on resize (stacked < 100 cols)
├── tabs.py      # ColumnTabs: add/remove/next/prev/select(n) via swap-pane with stash; border title rendering
├── keys.py      # keymap (single source) → tmux bind-key + hint-bar text + F1 help content
└── tandem.tmux.conf  # generated: mouse on, pane-border-status top, pane-border-format, status-format hints
```

```text
tmux -L tandem session "tandem"
├── window 0 "main"
│   ├── pane A  left column   (visible planner)
│   ├── pane B  right column  (visible implementer)
│   └── pane S  status app    (tandem's own Textual process)
└── window 1 "stash" (hidden) — background agents; swapped into A/B on tab switch
```

## UI Mockups
See impl.md "Main layout" and "Small terminal". Column border title formats:
```text
─ PLANNERS ─ [1 claude·opus]  2 agy·argon  ⚠3 agy·flash(exited 1) ─────
─ ▶ IMPLEMENTERS ─ [1 claude·sonnet]  2 + ─────────────────────────────   (▶ = focused column)
```
Help popup (F1, `tmux display-popup` running tandem's help screen):
```text
┌ tandem help ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Columns   F7 / F8      focus planners / implementers     │
│ Tabs      F3 / F4      previous / next agent in column   │
│           Alt+1…9      jump to agent N (if no conflict)  │
│ Agents    F2           add agent     F9  close agent     │
│ Status    F5 status    F6 queries                        │
│ Mouse     click pane to focus · drag border to resize    │
│           scroll wheel scrolls output                    │
│ Quit      F10 (asks; agents keep running if you detach)  │
│                                     [Esc] close          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
- **States Covered**: first run (auto-open the help popup once, then remember the dismissal in tandem's own state file), empty column placeholder pane, agent exited (pane stays open with `remain-on-exit`, border shows the exit code, `R` restart / `X` close prompt in tandem's placeholder), terminal resize (reflow to stacked layout), re-attach to an existing tandem session, quit confirm (detach vs kill all).
- **Interaction Notes**: key choices are final only after the **key-conflict audit** (below). The hint bar always shows the current key set. Mouse: focus, resize, scroll. Clicking the border tab labels is a stretch goal: implement it if `MouseDown1Border` + `mouse_x` resolve reliably, else document it as unsupported.
- **Accessibility Notes**: the focused column is marked with `▶` plus a bold border (not color alone). Hints are plain text.

## Implementation Notes
Changed files (`agent-workspace-package/tandem`): NEW `src/tandem/tmux/{__init__,client,keys,tabs,layout}.py`, `src/tandem/{commands,cli}.py` (cli now has subcommands), `src/tandem/config.py` (+`tmux_pane`, `workspace`, `state_dir`), `src/tandem/coordination/store.py` (+`write_session`, `remove_session`), placeholder `src/tandem/status/app.py` (replaced in t-007); tests `test_tmux_{client,keys,tabs,integration}.py`, `test_tos_guard.py`, `test_conf.py`, `test_commands.py`.

Decisions:
- **No libtmux.** A ~60-line `TmuxClient` over `subprocess` with an injectable runner was enough (task asked to record this).
- **Default-deny allow-list** in `TmuxClient.run`: `send-keys`, `capture-pane`, `pipe-pane`, buffers, `copy-mode`, `run-shell`, `if-shell`, unknown commands raise `ToSViolation`. `send_keys_own` / `capture_own` exist for tandem-owned panes only and fail closed by reading the pane's `@tandem_kind` tmux option (anything but `own` is refused). The only call site is the status-pane tab switch.
- **Pane state lives in tmux**, not in memory: each pane carries `@tandem_{kind,role,index,label,session,argv}` user options, so every `tandem tab|focus|close-agent|...` invocation (run from key bindings) is stateless.
- **Tabs via swap-pane**: each background agent gets its own hidden window (`stash-<role>-<n>`); a single stash window with repeated splits would run out of space after a few agents. Closing the last visible agent respawns the pane as a placeholder.
- Dedicated socket (`-L tandem`) and tandem-owned config file; the user's `~/.tmux.conf` is never loaded. `prefix None` so tmux eats no keys; `remain-on-exit on` keeps exited agents visible with the exit code in the border.
- Border title is a tmux format string; the focus marker `▶` is a tmux conditional (`#{?pane_active,▶ ,}`), and tab labels are restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._:· -]` so they cannot inject format syntax.
- Stacked layout (< 100 cols) uses `move-pane`, triggered by the `client-resized` hook; `pane-died` hook refreshes titles.
- **Workspace pinning:** popups and `run-shell` jobs start in the pane's cwd, which differs for implementers in worktrees. Bound commands are wrapped as `env TANDEM_WORKSPACE=<abs path> python -m tandem ...` so every pane agrees on the workspace and coordination store (found and fixed during smoke testing).
- Restart is **F11** instead of the mockup's `R`: binding a plain letter would require forwarding it to live AI panes with `send-keys`, which the ToS guard forbids.
- First-run help: a `client-attached` hook runs `tandem first-run`, which opens the help popup once and records a marker in tandem's state dir (hook registration is tested; the popup itself was not seen in a real client).

### Key-conflict audit (partial, stated honestly)
| Source | Finding |
|---|---|
| tmux defaults | Prefix removed (`prefix None`), so no tmux chord consumes keys. Root-table bindings are F1-F11 only. |
| claude 2.1.x | Documented chords are Ctrl/Alt/Shift based (Ctrl+C/D/L/R/O/B/T/G, Shift+Tab, Esc Esc, Alt+P/T); no F-key defaults known. Not re-verified against `/keybindings` in this session. |
| agy 1.3.x | Key defaults are not enumerated by `agy --help`; no F-key defaults known. Unverified. |
| macOS terminals | On laptops F1-F12 are media keys unless `fn` is held or "Use F1, F2 as standard function keys" is on. **Known usability limitation**, document in README (t-009). |
Result: all tandem bindings are bare F-keys (a test asserts no `C-`/`M-` chords). Residual risk: unknown agy F-key use.

## Validation
- Tests first for client, keys, tabs; integration tests then written against a real tmux (installed tmux 3.8 via Homebrew for this task).
- `uv run pytest`: 193 passed, including 13 real-tmux integration tests (build/positions, tags, hint bar, add/step/select tabs, session registry pane ids, close visible/last agent, placeholder replacement, exit code in border, restart, reflow stack/unstack, focus). `mypy --strict` clean.
- ToS guard tests: forbidden commands rejected at runtime; source grep confirms `send-keys`/`capture-pane`/`pipe-pane` appear only in `tmux/client.py`; no `shell=True`; no network modules.
- Smoke test through the real CLI (`tandem tab prev`, `focus implementer`, `close-agent` with `TMUX_PANE` set) against a live session: all exit 0 and state changed as expected.
- **Not validated:** an interactive attached session (pressing F1/F2/F9/F10 with a real client, mouse focus/resize, popup rendering, the quit menu, first-run popup) and running real `claude`/`agy` panes. The manual validation bullet is therefore only partly done; flag for the user to try `./run.sh` once.

## Security Review
Self-audit: default-deny tmux allow-list with fail-closed own-pane check; pane ids regex-validated before use; argv passed as list (tmux execs directly); `-e` env limited to four TANDEM_* keys (restart re-derives them, not copied from the pane); labels sanitized for tmux formats; stored `@tandem_argv` JSON validated as `list[str]` before respawn. Residual: processes in an AI pane run as the same user and could call tmux themselves; the guard constrains tandem, not the agents.
